findings.summary: The quiet path must still print refusal lines, and the plan should say so.
findings.evidence: `propose` prints refusal lines before checking whether any proposal was generated. The plan says the automatic path is silent when nothing repeats and prints only when proposals are written or refused. That works only if the quiet flag suppresses just the 'no class has repeated' line. Fix: State that the quiet flag removes only the 'no class has repeated across enough distinct jobs' line. Keep the refusal lines and the 'proposed default' lines.

findings.summary: `RealSteps::records()` returns `Records`, and it is not shown whether that type carries DefaultsProposal records.
findings.evidence: `queue()` uses `self.records()` of type `Records`. `proposals: Vec<ProposalRecord>` is declared in store.rs:225 and introspect.rs:272. `accept_proposal` and `pending` use `GitRecords::load`. The plan leaves this choice to the producer. Fix: Have the helper use `open(&GitRecords::load(...).proposals)`, the same source `pending()` uses, so that queue() and accept_proposal_in_limit read the same set.

findings.summary: `accept_proposal` runs the reader through `ask`, so the real-steps drain test needs the stub reader agent that the existing drain and steward tests use.
findings.evidence: proposals.rs:642 calls `self.ask(&accept_request(&pending), ui)`. Without a fake agent, the test would hit a real reader or fail at approve, and would then show the proposal as 'could not be approved' instead of Accepted. Fix: Name the fixture's fake reader in step 6, and assert the drain report shows 'approved <proposal id> → <job>'.

findings.summary: The phrase 'a drain test confirms Steps::propose has no error path' shows only a type signature, not a behavior.
findings.evidence: A `()` return type is wiring. The closure-seam unit test is the behavioral proof. Fix: Drop that clause, or replace it with a counting stub whose propose prints a failure line, and assert that drain still returns its report.

summary: I read drain.rs, proposals.rs, introspect.rs and work_decisions.rs, and the round-3 plan matches the code. `Athena::propose` (proposals.rs:552) and `accept_proposal` (proposals.rs:638) exist. `accept_proposal` returns the same `reading::Proposal` type as `approve_in_limit` (work_decisions.rs:341), so `RealSteps::approve` (drain.rs:1594) can return an Approval through either path. `approve_all` (drain.rs:833) works over plain `Waiting` ids and does its room and budget checks per item, so proposals listed in `approvable` get the existing job-limit and budget checks. `introspect_job` and `introspect_intervention` (introspect.rs:1211-1229) are the never-failing wrappers built on `settle`, so hooking in after the record is stored cannot fail the introspection. `drain_with` (drain.rs:1159) calls `steps.queue()` first, so adding `steps.propose()` before it is a simple insertion. `role_limit` and `may_change` already give the ladder rule. The demonstrations check behavior: a proposal appears with no separate command, no repeat, status lists it, and drain accepts or holds it by the limit. Each would fail without the hook. The findings below are minor.
